appended a create record for T-0078
E034 PROTOCOL.md declared (population, 8 pre-named tags, 3 matched arms, gates A1-A4/B1, kill gate A4) before any fetch of the declared population
appended a claim record for T-0078

E034 reported: pooled tail 0.1352 vs Active tab 0.0303 (4.5x, replicates F055), per-tag 0.0000-0.4300 with both extremes replicating out of sample; D6 (tag/site attribution) and B1 (the answer-existed mechanism) both fail; F057, D063, D064 recorded

The canonical edge is unreachable from this host through nine named channels, which closes E033's open question 'what to measure recurrence on' on its other half: the label is available and the edge is not. Added to E033's five: the question's own comments, the answer's closed_details, a browser User-Agent on two hosts, both StackPrinter hosts, and SEDE.

A3a/A3b and both matched-n variants fire: pooled tail 0.1352 CI95 [0.1122,0.1620] against the Active tab's 0.0303 [0.0201,0.0455] and the score head's 0.0371, 4.5x, replicating F055 on an independent tag-stratified population. A4 kill gate fires (7 tags clear n>=50, 12 disjoint pairs) and AMENDMENT-1 R1 replicates both extremes out of sample. D6 fails: within-site tag pairs separate 4/10 against 14/26 cross-site, so tag and site are not apportioned. B1 fails: CI95 [-0.0774,+0.3075] on the no-accepted-answer share, so 'the answer existed and was not found' is not separable from 'a moderator closed it'. The declared a-priori stratum hypothesis is backwards. Established: where the repeats sit. Not established: what happened to them, or whether the spread is a tag.

PROTOCOL.md AMENDMENT-2, written after the run: the R2 gate declared in AMENDMENT-1 section 7 was ill-formed before the fetch (both branches returned true), so section 7 is left as declared and the amendment names the fix instead. D064.

The full suite caught its own gate on the way: test_decision_files refused DECISIONS-SCREENING-6.md because three separate lists name this repository's decision files (paths.MISSION_RECORDS, the test's own tuple, and reconcile.IMPLICATIONS['decision']) and all three were updated. That is the gate the file exists for -- a recorded decision would otherwise satisfy a gate by changing nothing.

The refactor that split reask.py and tally.py in two introduced a real defect, found by re-running the gates: reask.load() returns every sample, so the declared gates absorbed the R1 replication and reported it back as the result (pooled tail 0.1582 against the true 0.1352, every interval still plausible). measures.build() now reads the declared sample explicitly and asserts no amendment row is present, and falsify.py carries the mutation that puts the bug back. 45 checks, 17 mutations, all caught.

git add -A && git commit -q -m "D063/D064: an enumerated field is a set of literals and an absent key must mean inapplicable; a gate about a relation is a partition or a statistic

Two decisions from E034, in DECISIONS-SCREENING-6.md. D063: closed_reason carries ten
literals and exact duplicate (9 rows) is the legacy spelling of Duplicate (225), so every
enumeration rate in this record is a floor -- including E033 published 0.0540. D064: the
R2 gate E034 declared before its fetch asked whether one tag was disjoint from BOTH math
tags and overlapping A math tag; both were true, so it could not return one answer. The
fix is a count over the whole relation, not a predicate over a chosen subset.
